newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef traded higher on light to moderate demand and generally moderate offerings early in the week, USDA said. Most retail interest was for immediate needs, while most of the higher prices were generally paid late in the week. Also very light forwarded interest was noted both in the retail and HRI areas.

Processors again paid more for their live cattle needs, consequently these additional costs were passed on to the retailer and demand turned very light at the higher price levels as the week progressed.

Most primal cuts traded at firmer price levels, but the most gains were in the inside round cuts, tenderloins and some rib cuts as the week progressed. Closely trimmed items also experienced fairly good price gains, while the most price gains were in the Select cuts.

Beef trimmings were generally steady during the trading period with light to moderate demand and offerings. Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items were steady to firm on mostly moderate demand and offerings.

For the week - Select and Choice rib primal 1.50 to 3.00 higher; Select and Choice chuck primal 1.00 to 2.00 higher; Select and Choice round primal 1.50 to 2.50 higher; Select and Choice loin primal 2.50 to 4.00 higher; Closely trimmed items 1.50 to 2.50 higher; Beef trimmings generally steady; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items generally 1.00 higher.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up 1.47 at 97.61; 700/850 Up 1.98 at 97.38; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up 1.79 at 94.40; 700/850 Up 2.56 at 94.05.

COW AND BULL CARCASS, BONELESS PROCESSING BEEF, CUTTER COW CUTOUT The lean boneless beef market was forced higher this week, despite light to moderate grinding demand. Many cow killers curtailed slaughter receipts because of continually increasing live costs.

Lower lean percentage boneless beef moved at generally steady prices on light to moderate demand and offerings. The Utility cow carcass market also traded higher due to fairly light offerings and light to moderate demand. Furthermore, the cow cuts market traded higher on light offerings, especially the 100% lean items as demand was good.
Utility carcasses 2.00-4.00 higher; Cutter carcasses not established; 90% boneless beef 3.50-4.50 higher; 85% 1.50-2.00 higher; 75% firm to 3.00 higher; 65% generally steady.
The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Thursday, February 20, 1997 was estimated at 73.55 per cwt, up 3.03 from a week ago Friday.
